PullRequest.Title: agentHost: declare initiatorType on restricted engine snapshots
PullRequest.Body:

## What and why

Follow-up to #346455 (merged), which declared the per-call metadata the Copilot runtime will attach to restricted `engine.messages` and `engine.messages.length` snapshots. Those fields still cannot tell the call that starts a user's turn from the agent's follow-up calls in the same conversation.

A follow-up runtime update adds `initiatorType` to these snapshots: `user` or `agent`, with the same values and meaning as `initiatorType` on the runtime's model response event.

- **Declares `initiatorType`** in the `AgentHostRestrictedEngineCall` fragment. The router already passes runtime properties through unchanged, so the field flows as soon as the runtime sends it. Older runtimes omit it, and the router leaves it absent.
- **Documents the field** in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/AGENTS.md`.

Related to microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10632.

## Scope

No new event, destination, consent check or content-exclusion change, and no runtime code change in the Agent Host. Until the runtime dependency is updated, nothing new is sent.

## How to test

```text
pnpm run test-node --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostRestrictedTelemetry.test.ts
```

Result: **31 passing**. The per-call metadata test now also checks `initiatorType` in the upload envelopes: `user` on a root call, `agent` on a subagent call, and absent for a call from an older runtime.

```text
pnpm run eslint src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.test.ts
```

Result: **passed**.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restricted Copilot engine snapshot routing for root and subagent model calls (`engine.messages` and `engine.messages.length`)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each runtime notification enters `_routeGitHubTelemetry`, awaits restricted-telemetry account context resolution and `multiplexProperties`, then dispatches telemetry. The enhanced-GitHub HTTP POST is fire-and-forget and is not on the model-response/rendering critical path. The diff changes only GDPR schema documentation plus tests; it adds no executable step to this path, and `event.properties` already passed through unchanged before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve account telemetry policy via `/copilot_internal/user` discovery when the per-token cache is cold or near expiry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced discovery for concurrent callers per token on a cold/refreshing cache; zero network calls on a warm cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same context lookup and per-token coalescing occurred for every targeted restricted notification before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry routing waits for this context before deciding whether to emit, but the model-response/rendering path is not changed by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy notification properties, gzip/chunk configured long values, and JSON-serialize an Application Insights envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per targeted notification before sink dispatch; gzip is only performed for existing long/always-compressed properties. `initiatorType` is bounded and was already included through the pre-existing `...event.properties` spread when supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pre-diff routing already spread all runtime properties and serialized the same supplied `initiatorType` value; the changed GDPR fragment is static schema metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Multiplexing completes before telemetry routing returns; envelope serialization precedes the fire-and-forget POST. The diff adds no runtime property copy, compression, or serialization work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST an enhanced restricted telemetry envelope to the configured telemetry endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fire-and-forget POST per eligible `engine.messages` or `engine.messages.length` notification; no retries. Event count is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notification already produced the same POST and already carried all supplied runtime properties through the property spread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is started after serialization but is not awaited, so delivery is off the telemetry route's completion critical path and off the user interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Log internal-only `engine.messages.length` telemetry through the OneDataSystem appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One appender log per eligible length notification for an internal account; none for non-internal accounts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Internal length-event logging had identical cardinality and placement before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Logging is invoked synchronously, with downstream transmission owned by the appender; the diff does not add or move this call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of runtime engine notifications across root and child model calls. Effective cardinality remains one routing/serialization operation per notification, one enhanced-GitHub upload for each eligible notification, and an additional internal sink emission only for eligible `engine.messages.length` notifications from internal accounts. The added bounded `initiatorType` value does not change event count or effective grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Account discovery is coalesced per GitHub token through the cached in-flight promise. Warm context reads require no network request. Notification routing awaits multiplexing, while enhanced-GitHub uploads are fire-and-forget; there is no new limiter, queue, fan-out, or concurrency introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Restricted telemetry context is cached per token and concurrent cold requests share one discovery promise; warm reads reuse the entry until its refresh window. This PR changes no cache key, hit/miss behavior, invalidation, negative-cache behavior, or coalescing. Older runtimes omit `initiatorType`; newer runtime properties were already spread by the router before this declaration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only production TypeScript change is inside a GDPR comment fragment, while executable routing demonstrably spreads `event.properties` wholesale both before and after the PR. Tests and documentation do not execute in the product path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend schema retention may determine whether curators can consume the field, but it does not alter client-side event cardinality, serialization placement, payload construction, or boundary calls. Runtime dependency updates are explicitly outside this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR declares an already-pass-through bounded metadata field for schema purposes and updates tests/docs; it introduces no runtime CPU, allocation, I/O, network, concurrency, cache, or lifecycle mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced the engine-snapshot telemetry path through context discovery, multiplexing, serialization, enhanced-GitHub POSTs, and internal telemetry. No executable production behavior changes, so no performance finding or regression-fix record is warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
